title: Renewal momentum briefing and sticky decision grid
content:
PURPOSE
This lightweight facilitation runbook is for 30–60 minute QBRs where the primary goal is to: 1) calibrate executive-level renewal momentum, 2) get a committed next-step (three-anchor ask), and 3) identify and triage any technical or commercial escalations that would block renewal.

AUDIENCE
- Customer Success Manager (CSM) leading the meeting
- Customer executive sponsor(s) (VP/Director level)
- Technical owner (CTO/Eng lead) optional depending on risk
- Product or Solutions Eng (as needed for technical deep dives)

ONE-LINER TO OPEN THE MEETING
"We have 30 minutes today to surface the signals that matter for renewal, confirm one concrete next-step that advances momentum, and capture any risk we need to de-risk in the next 30 days."

AGENDA (30m template)
- 0:00–0:02 Quick welcome + objective (CSM)
- 0:02–0:08 Executive health snapshot (CSM) — 3 slides / 2 bullets each (usage, business impact, 30d asks)
- 0:08–0:16 Sticky decision grid — surface 3 candidate asks and recommend one (CSM + customer)
- 0:16–0:24 Risk surfacing & mitigation commitments (technical/product owners)
- 0:24–0:28 Align on next-step owner & timeline (CSM)
- 0:28–0:30 Close: parking lot & follow-ups (CSM)

FACILITATION SCRIPT (compact prompts)
- Opening (0:00–0:02): "Quick purpose — leave with a concrete next step that moves us closer to renewal. If anything else needs follow-up, we'll capture and assign it."
- Health snapshot (0:02–0:08): present 3 metrics: active requests/day, 99th percentile latency, cost per 1k tokens. For each: "So what does this tell us about your business outcome?" Pause for 15–30s response.
- Introduce sticky decision grid (0:08): "We’ll propose three asks that would move momentum — pick which you want to commit to today, or tell us what’s missing."
- When a risk is raised: mirror it back and ask "What would make this safe to move forward?" (capture the smallest unblock)
- Closing (0:24–0:30): "Who owns the ask, what is the timeline, and what will success look like in 30 days?"

STICKY DECISION GRID (how to use)
- Purpose: convert options into a single prioritized ask (the sticky ask) the customer can commit to during the meeting.
- Columns to prepare ahead: Option name | Business impact (quantified) | Customer effort | Redwood effort | Risk (0–5) | Recommended ask

Sample filled grid (example items)
1) Increase dedicated capacity (1 GPU pool) | Impact: +20% throughput, reduces time-to-insight | Customer effort: Low (approve order) | Redwood effort: Medium (provision) | Risk: 2 | Recommended ask: Approve PO for dedicated capacity this month
2) Production integration of auditing logs | Impact: Required for compliance gate | Customer effort: High (internal security sign-off) | Redwood effort: Low | Risk: 4 | Recommended ask: Commit to security review by dd/mm
3) Feature gating to reduce token use by 25% | Impact: Lower costs ~15% | Customer effort: Medium (config changes) | Redwood effort: Low | Risk: 1 | Recommended ask: Agree to test flagged routes for 2 weeks

DECISION GUIDE (CSM heuristics)
- If risk >= 4: don’t make it the sticky ask unless there is a known remediation plan + owner in the meeting.
- Prefer asks that: are low friction for the customer, have measurable business impact in 30 days, and are owned by a named individual.
- If customer is ambivalent, propose a time-boxed trial as the sticky ask.

PRE-MEETING CHECKLIST (CSM) - pull these 24–48 hours before
- Usage dashboard: last 90 days token counts, top 10 API routes by volume
- Error & latency trends: 95th/99th, incidents in last 30 days
- Cost breakdown: cost per route / projected monthly run rate
- Adoption signals: #active users, sessions/week, new features used
- Contract/renewal dates, current committed capacity, outstanding invoices
- Recent support tickets and SRE escalations (list IDs)
- Current open product requests and their owners

PRE-MEETING CHECKLIST (ENGINEERING/PRODUCT)
- Validate the 99th pctl latency and any known regressions
- Prepare a short mitigation plan for top technical risk (one slide)
- Confirm any capacity changes are provisionable in the requested timeframe

RISK SNAPSHOT (one-pager template to share in meeting)
- Technical risks (top 3): regression in 99th pctl, tokenization mismatch, KV cache footprint causing OOM
- Commercial risks (top 3): cost run-rate above budget, procurement delays, compliance gating
- Customer-side mitigations: known hiring freeze, pending security posture review, integration backlog
- Redwood mitigations: temporary rate-limits, scoped quantization profile, audit-support packet

QUICK DATA QUERIES (copy-paste)
- Usage by route (last 30d): SELECT route, SUM(tokens) FROM usage WHERE customer_id = X AND ts >= now() - 30d GROUP BY route ORDER BY SUM(tokens) DESC LIMIT 10;
- Latency trend (7d, p95/p99): queries to APM/observability for p95/p99 per hour
- Cost forecast (next 30d): use billing projection script: scripts/billing/proj --customer X --window 30

ESCALATION PATHS (if meeting surfaces an urgent blocker)
- Priority A (security/compliance block): page Solutions Eng -> Security -> Account Exec. Response SLA: 24–48h for initial plan.
- Priority B (performance regression): page SRE on-call -> provide baseline, enable debug logs. Response SLA: 8–24h to triage.
- Priority C (commercial/legal): escalate to Sales Ops / Legal; CSM to own comms.

DOCUMENTING DECISIONS (what CSM should capture live)
- Sticky ask (exact language)
- Owner (name + email)
- Target date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Success metric(s) (how we'll validate in 30 days)
- If blocked: blocker description + next-step to remove blocker + owner

SAMPLE CLOSING LINE (phone/email follow-up)
"Thanks — based on today we agreed to [sticky ask]. I’ll send a one-page follow-up with the owner and dates by EOD. If the technical team needs runway, we’ll flag an SRE deep-dive within 48 hours."

MEETING NOTES TEMPLATE (copy into meeting doc)
- Date: 
- Attendees: 
- Executive health snapshot (3 bullets): 
- Sticky ask selected: 
- Owner / due date: 
- Risks captured (top 3): 
- Follow-up items (owner + due date): 

POST-MEETING 48H CHECK (CSM cadence)
- Send summary and owner assignments (within 6 hours)
- Confirm capacity changes are queued with infra (if applicable)
- Validate one data point that shows progress (e.g., trial started, PO submitted)
- If no traction in 7 days, schedule follow-up 15m touch with exec sponsor

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS (work-in-progress)
- Consider adding a short "momentum thermometer" slide for execs (green/amber/red) with explicit criteria.
- Need to standardize 3 default sticky asks by segment (SMB, Midmarket, Enterprise).
- Pilot the grid with two accounts next quarter and capture success rate to refine heuristics.
